The cause is in the driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)):

- In [`explicit_confirm`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), line 161 checks `re.search(r"\bi confirmed\b", t)` instead of `r"\bi confirm\b"` (as in [`lab23_dcitl.py.orig`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig#L151-L162), line 156; `scripts/port_dcitl.py --check` also reports this single-line mismatch).
- When a patient says `"I confirm"`, `explicit_confirm` returns `None` (it also does not match `^(yes|yep|yeah|confirmed)\b`). Under `consent_in_code=True` (`DcitlF`), [`Driver.consent`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271) ignores a model `"yes"` and returns `None`, so [`Driver.unclear`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L297-L306) re-asks for confirmation and hands off to staff on the second unclear reply (`n >= 2`).

Because the cause is in `clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py`, this is a `finding` (no files were modified).
